title: The 1945 Vietnamese declaration quotes the American and French rights sentences and then declares Vietnam free
summary: Ho's 1945 declaration quotes the American and French rights lines and declares Vietnam free.
body: The 2 September 1945 declaration, as Fordham prints it, quotes 'all men are created equal' and the French declaration, and then says the members of the Provisional Government solemnly declare that Vietnam has the right to be a free and independent country. The text uses other empires' rights language against French rule. It is not the American declaration. The wording on the page includes: "Government of the Democratic Republic of Vietnam, solemnly declare to the world that Vietnam has the right to be a free and independent country-and in fact is so already. The entire Vietnamese people are determined to mobilize all their physical and mental strength, to sacrifice their lives and property in order to safeguard their independence and liberty. Source: Ho Chi". The evidence label is the truth-gate ceiling for this host. The host is not on the gate's primary-text or official list, so the label is weak. The quotation is still the page's wording.
said_by: Provisional Government of the Democratic Republic of Vietnam, Fordham
